body:
weight: light
tier: 0
charter: C4

Build the kill switch per SPEC-v0.2 'Kill switch' and 'Summoner'. `factory/HALT` on `main`: present means every loop sleeps 30 minutes and checks again. Adding it is a one-line PR needing zero approvals; removing it needs two (CODEOWNERS + a branch ruleset keyed on deletion). The halt also sets the `factory:halt` label so the summoner fires a halt notice.

Acceptance criteria (verified by `make test`, offline):
1. `halt-check.sh` exits 0 when `factory/HALT` is absent from `origin/main` (checked with `git ls-tree origin/main factory/HALT` after a fetch, never the working tree) and exits 3 with the sleep interval on stdout when present; verified by tests/test_halt.sh cases 'absent' and 'present' against a local bare origin.
2. `apply-branch-protection.sh` is dry-run by default and prints every `gh api` call it would make from factory/policy/branch-protection.json; with `--apply` it makes them; idempotent (a second run is a no-op); verified by case 'dry-run-prints-calls' using the fake gh.
3. `summon.sh --kind halt|needs-approval|needs-acceptance` posts exactly one Discord-webhook message naming one human, the ticket id, the decision needed and a link, and refuses any other kind with exit 2; verified by tests/test_summon.sh with a fake curl capturing the payload.
4. `.github/workflows/summoner.yml` fires on the `factory:halt` label and on a push to main that touches `factory/HALT` only; verified by case 'workflow-triggers' (a grep assertion documented in the test).
5. tests/test_layout.sh keeps asserting `factory/HALT` is absent from the tree on main.

Out of scope: the Discord webhook secret itself (the repo owner sets `SUMMONER_WEBHOOK`); the daily digest (build order 4).
title: Implement the kill switch: halt-check, branch rules as code, halt notice
